mission_10: Federated learning security is critical because the open participation model makes FL vulnerable to poisoning attacks. Data poisoning corrupts local training data by flipping labels or injecting backdoor patterns, causing the global model to learn incorrect associations. Model poisoning is more dangerous: malicious clients craft updates specifically designed to degrade the global model or implant backdoors. This mission implements both attacks and two defenses. Krum is a Byzantine-robust aggregation rule that selects the update closest to its neighbors, effectively ignoring outliers. Outlier detection uses cosine similarity to identify updates that point in significantly different directions from the majority. Real-world FL systems must defend against both accidental failures and malicious attacks, making security a core component of any production deployment.
